words: The universe encompasses all spacetime, so its contingent existence requires an explanation beyond physical spacetime, inferred to be a transcendent personal cause.
critique: Strongest feature: Grounding the argument in the universe as all spacetime yields an inference that its contingent explanation must be external, transcendent, and nonphysical, directly supporting a divine cause. Principal limitation: Transcendence follows from locating the explanation beyond space and time, but neither the universe's contingency nor the transition from nonphysical to personal is established, weakening evidence warrant and calibration. Live burden: Pro must defend contingency and demonstrate why the required external explanation entails agency, while excluding impersonal transcendent alternatives capable of explaining spacetime without personhood. Locked score: The exact score of 74 fits because responsiveness and relevance are strong through direct contact with the central explanatory burden, whereas evidence warrant and calibration remain weaker despite precision and clarity keeping the inference intelligible.
